rules.title: California Daily Overtime (Labor Code §510)

result.summary: 1.5x regular rate for hours over 8 in a day

rules.title: California Double Time (Labor Code §510)

result.summary: 2x regular rate for hours over 12 in a day

rules.title: Federal Weekly Overtime (FLSA)

result.summary: 1.5x regular rate for hours over 40 in a week

rules.title: Federal Workweek Definition (FLSA)

result.summary: Overtime is computed over a fixed and regularly recurring period of 168 hours (seven consecutive 24-hour periods) that may begin on any day and hour; it may be changed only permanently and not to evade overtime, and hours may not be averaged across weeks

rules.title: California Workday and Workweek Definition

result.summary: Daily overtime is measured over a fixed 24-hour workday and weekly and seventh-day overtime over a fixed 168-hour workweek, each starting at a time the employer sets and changes only for legitimate business reasons

rules.title: California Seventh Consecutive Day: 1.5x for the First 8 Hours (Labor Code §510)

result.summary: The first 8 hours worked on the seventh consecutive day of work in a workweek are paid at 1.5x the regular rate (AB 60, effective 2000-01-01). Does not apply to employees on a valid alternative workweek schedule.

rules.title: California Seventh Consecutive Day: 2x After 8 Hours (Labor Code §510)

result.summary: Hours over 8 on the seventh consecutive day of work in a workweek are paid at 2x the regular rate.

rules.title: Federal — EAP Exemption Salary Level $684/week (29 CFR 541.600)

result.summary: An executive, administrative or professional employee is exempt from FLSA overtime only if paid on a salary basis at least $684 a week ($35,568 a year), plus $107,432 total annual compensation for the highly compensated employee test. The 2024 rule raising these levels was vacated (E.D. Tex. 2024-11-15) and formally rescinded by DOL on 2026-05-15, so the 2019 levels remain in force. States may set higher thresholds.

rules.title: California — Exempt Salary Threshold $1,352/week (2x Minimum Wage), 2026

params.basis: 2 x state minimum wage ($16.90) x 40 hours; indexed annually

result.summary: Executive, administrative and professional employees are exempt only if paid a monthly salary of at least twice the state minimum wage for full-time employment (Labor Code §515(a)): $1,352 a week / $5,858.67 a month / $70,304 a year at the 2026 minimum wage of $16.90. Health care and large fast-food employers covered by industry minimum wages use twice that wage ($1,600 a week at $20). Rises each January with the minimum wage.

rules.title: California Reporting Time Pay (half scheduled shift, min 2 hrs, max 4 hrs)

result.summary: Half the scheduled shift hours at regular rate (minimum 2 hours, maximum 4 hours)

rules.title: California Second Reporting Time Pay (minimum 2 hours)

result.summary: Pay for minimum 2 hours at regular rate for second reporting in one workday

rules.title: California Split Shift Premium (+1 hr at state minimum wage)

result.summary: 1 additional hour at the state minimum wage rate (unless total daily earnings already exceed min wage × (hours worked + 1))

rules.title: California First Meal Break (>5 hours)

result.summary: 30-minute meal break for shifts of 5+ hours

rules.title: California — Meal Break Required (shifts > 5 hrs)

result.summary: California requires a 30-minute meal break for shifts over 5 hours. Ensure a break is scheduled.

rules.title: California Second Meal Break (>10 hours)

result.summary: 30-minute meal break for shifts of 10+ hours

rules.title: California — First Meal Period May Be Waived on Shifts of 6 Hours or Less

result.summary: When the total work period is no more than 6 hours the first meal period may be waived by mutual consent of employer and employee (Labor Code §512(a)). The consent need not be written but should be documented; the employee may withdraw it.

rules.title: California — First Meal Period Cannot Be Waived on Shifts Over 6 Hours (On-Duty Meal Only by Written Agreement)

result.summary: A first meal period on a shift longer than 6 hours cannot be waived. A paid on-duty meal period is permitted only when the nature of the work prevents relief from all duty and the parties have a written agreement that the employee may revoke at any time (Wage Orders §11). Otherwise a missed or late meal period owes one hour of premium pay (§226.7).

rules.title: California — Second Meal Period May Be Waived on Shifts of 10 to 12 Hours

result.summary: When the total work period is more than 10 but no more than 12 hours the second meal period may be waived by mutual consent, but only if the first meal period was not waived (Labor Code §512(a)). On shifts over 12 hours the second meal period cannot be waived outside the health care exception.

rules.title: Los Angeles — Offer Hours to Existing Employees Before Hiring

result.summary: Before hiring new employees or contractors, the employer must offer the work in writing to current employees for 72 hours (or until accepted) when they are qualified

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (offer of additional work) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — 14-Day Advance Notice Required (Retail)

result.summary: 1 hour of pay at the regular rate for each change the employer makes to a posted schedule with less than 14 days notice that adds time or changes the date, time or location with no loss of hours

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5, §185.00 et seq. (Fair Work Week Ordinance)
citations.section: LAMC Art. 5 (advance notice and predictability pay)

rules.title: Los Angeles — Schedule Change Premium (hours subtracted or shift cancelled with <14 days notice)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each hour not worked when, with less than 14 days notice, the employer reduces a shift by at least 15 minutes or cancels it

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (predictability pay) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — Good Faith Estimate at Hire

result.summary: Before hire, and within 10 days of a request, the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the employee's work schedule

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (good faith estimate) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — On-Call Shift Premium (not called in)

result.summary: Half the regular rate for each scheduled hour of an on-call shift the employee is not called in to work

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (predictability pay) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — Right to Decline Late-Added Hours

result.summary: The employee may decline any hours, shifts or changes not on the posted schedule or added with less than 14 days notice; the employee's consent to a change must be in writing

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5 (right to decline) (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: Los Angeles — Fair Work Week: Right to Request Hours, Times and Locations; Written Reason for Denial

result.summary: A covered retail employee may request a preference for certain hours, times or locations of work. The employer may accept or decline, but a denial must state the reason in writing. Employee-requested changes do not trigger predictability pay.

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5, §185.03 (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: California Lactation Accommodation

result.summary: Reasonable break time to express milk, running with paid rest breaks where possible and otherwise unpaid; a private non-bathroom space is required (space-only hardship exemption under 50 employees)

citations.source: Cal. Labor Code §§1030-1034 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: California Rest Break (10 min per 4 hours worked)

result.summary: 10-minute rest break for shifts of 3.5+ hours

rules.title: California — Rest Break Required (per 4 hrs worked)

result.summary: California requires a paid 10-minute rest break for every 4 hours worked. Ensure rest breaks are scheduled.

rules.title: Federal Lactation Break Time (PUMP Act)

result.summary: Reasonable break time each time the employee needs to express milk for one year after the child's birth, in a private non-bathroom space; unpaid unless the employee is not fully relieved or uses a paid break (employers under 50 may claim undue hardship)

citations.source: Fair Labor Standards Act §18d (PUMP for Nursing Mothers Act)

rules.title: California Day of Rest (1 day off per 7-day workweek)

result.summary: Scheduling an employee to work more than 6 consecutive days without a day of rest. Employee may voluntarily choose to work the 7th day. Exemptions for emergencies and certain industries.

rules.title: Los Angeles — 10-Hour Rest Period (Retail)

result.summary: 1.5x pay rate for hours worked within the 10-hour rest period

citations.source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Art. 5, §185.00 et seq. (Fair Work Week Ordinance)

rules.title: California Mini-WARN Act (60-day notice, 75+ employees)

result.summary: California requires 60 days advance written notice before plant closing or mass layoff affecting 75+ employees.

params.name: duration_months
params.description: How long after the child's birth the right lasts, in months (federal: 12); omitted when the law sets no limit

params.description: Employers below this size may claim undue hardship (federal: 50)

params.name: minimum_minutes
params.description: Paid minutes per break where the law sets a figure (New York: 30)

params.name: rest_hours

obligations.description: Before hiring new staff or using a staffing agency to cover hours, the employer must offer those hours to existing (part-time) employees.

params.description: How long the offer must stay open to existing employees before the employer may hire (72 hours = 3 days)

obligations.name: Rest between shifts (clopening)
obligations.description: A closing shift followed by an opening shift with less than the required rest is barred, or owes a premium, unless the employee consents.

params.name: rest_hours
params.description: Minimum hours between the end of one shift and the start of the next

params.name: amount
params.description: Premium amount, in the unit given

params.name: unit
params.description: How the premium is expressed

obligations.description: At hire (and on request or when circumstances change) the employer must give a written good faith estimate of the employee's expected hours, days and shifts.

params.name: lookback_days
params.description: Period the estimate is based on or must be revisited over, where the law sets one (Philadelphia and Chicago: 90 days)

obligations.name: Right to decline late-added hours
obligations.description: The employee may refuse hours or shifts the employer adds or moves inside the notice window; working them needs the employee's consent.

params.name: notice_days
params.description: Hours added with less than this much notice may be declined

obligations.name: Right to request schedule changes
obligations.description: The employee may ask for changes to hours, days, times, location or a flexible or predictable arrangement without retaliation; some laws also oblige the employer to consider, answer in writing, or grant the request absent a business reason.

params.description: Requests the employer must entertain per year

params.name: retaliation_only
params.description: True when the law only bars retaliation for asking

obligations.name: Mass layoff / plant closing notice (WARN)

params.name: employee_threshold

obligations.description: The lowest hourly rate an employer may pay a covered employee.
